evidence_title: Code of Alabama § 22-21B-3 Definitions (Alabama Health Care Rights of Conscience Act)
evidence_quote: HEALTH CARE PROVIDER. Any individual who may be asked to participate in any way in a health care service, including, but not limited to: A physician, ... pharmacist
notes: § 22-21B-4(a): provider "has the right not to participate" in a service violating conscience when objected in writing. Scope limited to abortion, human cloning, embryonic stem cell research and sterilization, incl. dispensing. Unofficial republication (onecle).

evidence_title: Ark. Code § 20-16-304 Policy--Authority (FindLaw, current as of Mar. 28, 2024)
evidence_quote: Nothing in this subchapter shall prohibit a physician, pharmacist, or any other authorized paramedical personnel from ... [refusing to furnish] contraceptive procedures, supplies, or information
notes: Also Ark. Code § 17-80-504 (Medical Ethics and Diversity Act) general conscience right per Guttmacher (Sept. 2026). NWLC (July 2025) lists AR among states explicitly allowing pharmacist refusal.

evidence_title: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 733 (FindLaw)
evidence_quote: A licentiate may decline to dispense a prescription drug or device on this basis only if the licentiate has previously notified their employer, in writing, of the drug or class of drugs to which the licentiate objects
notes: Stored false. Conditional conscience accommodation ("ethical, moral, or religious grounds"): requires prior written notice and employer accommodation without undue hardship; employer must ensure timely patient access. Coexists with § 733(a) duty not to obstruct.

evidence_title: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 25-6-102 (FindLaw, current as of Jan. 1, 2025)

notes: Declination allowed only for unlawful, harmful, fraudulent or non-legitimate prescriptions; no conscience exception. NWLC (July 2025) lists NV among duty-to-dispense states.

evidence_title: National Women's Law Center, Pharmacy Refusals 101 (fact sheet, July 2025)
evidence_quote: Eight states—CA, IL, ME, MA, NV, NJ, WA, WI— explicitly require pharmacists or pharmacies to provide medication to patients.
notes: State not among the eight with an explicit duty-to-dispense law/rule. Ohio Rev. Code § 4743.10 protects conscience refusals.
